solverDefinition: Runs the Minimum Vertex Cover 2-approximation solver and returns its cover if it has at most K nodes, otherwise returns {}. The 2-approximation solver is a naive solver for Vertex Cover that does not have a clear origination, although there have been many improvements upon it published. It repeatedly picks an arbitrary remaining edge, adds both endpoints to the cover, and removes all edges incident to either endpoint, until no edges remain. It returns a cover of size at most 2n when the optimal solution is n.
source: Cormen, Thomas H.; Leiserson, Charles E.; Rivest, Ronald L.; Stein, Clifford (2001) [1990]. 'Section 35.1: The vertex-cover problem'. Introduction to Algorithms (2nd ed.). MIT Press and McGraw-Hill. pp. 1024–1027. ISBN 0-262-03293-7.
